newsitem.title: UK: City of Moscow launches first international bond.
newsitem.headline: City of Moscow launches first international bond.

text.p: The City of Moscow launched its first international bond on Tuesday following an extensive global roadshow.
The $500 million May 2000 bond was priced to yield 315 basis points over the 6.375 percent May 2000 U.S. Treasury.
The size was larger than the $300-$400 million initially mooted.
The bond was priced at the tighter end of the 300-350 b.p. range over U.S. Treasury notes originally suggested.
The bond pays a coupon of 9.50 percent and there is a short first coupon on June 6, 1997.
Credit Suisse First Boston and Nomura are joint lead managers for the transaction.
Chairman of the committee for municipal loans & stock market Mechislav Klimovich recently said Moscow was limited to raise $500 million this year.
Moscow is rated Ba2 by Moody's Investors Service and BB- by Standard & Poor's.
